title: VMS / Drift
description: Per-camera input and output statistics against their reference, the drift detector against h, alarms, and injected onsets (tasks 9.1 to 9.4).

panels.title: Cameras alarming
panels.description: Cameras with at least one channel past h now (VmsCameraDrift). Above 0: follow RUNBOOK "Drift alerts", starting with the camera's row below.

panels.title: Cameras monitored
panels.description: Cameras with a finished reference, so with statistics and a detector. Fewer than the cameras sending means some are still calibrating (the first 60 s after a camera appears or is recalibrated).

panels.title: Calibrating
panels.description: Cameras whose reference period is still running: no statistics and no alarms yet. A camera stuck here never got enough frames; check the Pipeline dashboard.

panels.title: Alarm onsets in range
panels.description: Channel alarms started (0 to 1) over the dashboard's time range, summed over channels and cameras (one drift often trips several channels). Many onsets on a healthy site mean the calibration understates its normal variation: recalibrate it or raise h (RUNBOOK).

panels.title: Fewest frames per window
panels.description: The smallest number of processed frames in any selected camera's 30 s window (150 at 5 FPS). Under 20 the statistics are undefined and drift goes unseen: the camera stopped or the worker is behind.

panels.title: Detector h
panels.description: The decision threshold in clean-run standard deviations (D34: 10, 3x the largest clean value). Raising it trades detection delay for fewer false alarms; see the delay vs false-alarm plot (BENCHMARKS).

panels.title: Alarm by camera
panels.description: Red while any channel of the camera is past h. Blue markers are injected drift onsets (loadgen scenarios); the gap from a marker to red is the detection delay (5 to 30 s on the injected drifts, E-054).

panels.title: Detector statistic by camera
panels.description: Per camera, the largest channel statistic the detector compares with h (threshold: |z|, the window's distance from its reference in clean-run standard deviations; CUSUM: S). Log scale: clean cameras sit near 1, drifted ones at tens or hundreds.

panels.title: Detector statistic by channel
panels.description: The same statistic per channel, the largest over the selected cameras: which statistic moved. It names the symptom, not the cause: darkening also lowers noise, a camera shift reads as blur (RUNBOOK).

panels.title: Brightness
panels.description: Mean gray level (0 to 255). Falls with night, a dirty lens, a failing sensor or IR switching. Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Contrast
panels.description: Std of gray levels. Falls with fog, glare or a washed-out exposure. Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Sharpness
panels.description: ln(1 + variance of the Laplacian). Falls with defocus, a smeared or wet lens, motion blur, or a camera shift (fewer edges). Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Noise
panels.description: Noise estimate (Immerkaer). Rises with low light and high gain; darkening lowers it. Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Detections per frame
panels.description: Objects with confidence >= 0.25. Moves with traffic and with the model failing (blur, occlusion) or the scene changing. Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Mean confidence
panels.description: Mean detection confidence. Falls when the model is less sure: blur, noise, darkness it was not trained on. Solid: mean over the last 30 s window; dashed: the reference mean; shaded: the alarm band (window means where the threshold detector stays quiet, from the reference and the clean-run calibration). Leaving the band raises VmsCameraDrift; gaps mean too few frames or detections in the window.

panels.title: Confidence and class-mix distances
panels.description: The one-sided channels as z against h: KS and Wasserstein-1 between the window's and the reference's confidences, and PSI of the class mix (a new scene, or a model that confuses classes).

panels.title: Frames in window
panels.description: Processed frames and detections in the 30 s window. Below 20 frames or 20 detections the statistics are undefined (gaps above), which is VmsDriftNoData, not "no drift".
